notes: Muse is a FORK variant of checkpoint-rewind, like codex. Muse's Source is FilesUnderRoot(~/.local/share/muse/sessions): a single-birth adapter (no presession row -- session.jsonl materializes at session open, before any prompt, per the 1-1/2-1 sibling cells). The ORIGINAL session runs two normal turns (GAMMA, DELTA) -- the checkpoints to rewind from. /rewind then forks: a NEW session_id appears carrying session.fork.created{source_session_id=<original>}, restored from the rewound point (accepting the picker's default/most-recent candidate -- no arrow-key navigation needed, live-verified). The original session's row stays ready (the rewind itself derives no state_transition; every record it appends -- command.invoked, runtime.command_intake.*, session.started, session.end -- is Skip=true in parser.go, by design: process liveness, not this record, is what marks a session ended). The post-rewind turn runs on the NEW session from the rewound point. agent_supports=partial: /rewind reverts conversation state only -- the live confirmation dialog states verbatim 'Your files stay unchanged.' Provenance caveat (not asserted, not a bug): session.fork.created's source_session_id is not wired into the muse adapter (zero 'fork' references in core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/), so the daemon surfaces the fork as an independent new session_id rather than a parent-linked child -- the new row + arc are still observed, only the linkage LABEL is lost. Vacuous-pass guard: events.jsonl carries zero trace of the rewind, so 'a new session_id appeared' is asserted here only as new_session:true on a session_id gated by tight relative_to/max_delay_ms timing -- record's verify step additionally greps the raw session.jsonl for session.fork.created.source_session_id to positively confirm THIS cell's rewind produced the new row, not unrelated concurrent muse activity (a real risk: this assessment's own live probes observed 5+ unrelated concurrent muse sessions on the recording machine). KNOWN DRIVER GAP: driver-interactive.sh's resolve_transcript() never re-resolves TRANSCRIPT/UUID to the new forked session after /rewind (same class as the not_implemented reset_session step for /clear|/new) -- record must port a re-resolution primitive (mirroring codex driver-interactive.sh's swap_after_slash) before the v2_* phases below can be driven end to end; until then wait_turn for the post-rewind turn polls the stale original transcript and times out.

text: Muse's own session.jsonl materializes well under 1s after launch (single-birth, no presession row) -- session appears in ready
First user prompt ('GAMMA') drives ready -> working
First turn completes back to ready -- checkpoint 1
Second user prompt ('DELTA') drives ready -> working on the same session
Second turn completes back to ready -- checkpoint 2, the point to rewind back from

invariants: no state_transition to working on the original session_id
no transcript_removed for the original session_id
text: Spec: 'Session row reflects the rewound state with state ready' -- after /rewind the ORIGINAL session's row stays ready (the rewind itself is not a turn; command.invoked/runtime.command_intake.*/session.started/session.end are all Skip=true) and is never removed (muse emits no transcript_removed for it)

Spec: 'a linked new session_id if the adapter forks' -- /rewind materializes a fresh session_id never seen before, whose raw session.jsonl opens with session.fork.created{source_session_id=<original>} (checked by record's verify against the raw transcript, not events.jsonl -- see notes)

Spec: 'Subsequent turns start cleanly from the rewound point: ready -> working' -- resubmitting the pre-filled post-rewind prompt drives the NEW session ready -> working (must NOT match a stale working transition on the original session)
Spec: post-rewind turn completes back to ready on the NEW session -- a clean ready -> working -> ready arc from the rewound point; final live state is ready
